findings.observation: The complete spear remains visible, but the head tip and butt cap sit only about 4% from the nearest canvas edges, inside the required 8% safe margin.
Exactly one complete spear is present, with one connected head, shaft, grip wraps, and butt cap and no duplicate weapon or extra gear.
The long two-hand seasoned-wood shaft and distinct pointed metal thrusting head read immediately as a spear.
Although the socket aligns cleanly with the shaft, the very large broad winged head and exposed ornamental core appear excessively top-heavy for the narrow wooden haft and grounded two-hand use.
The bright metal spearhead supplies the only overt rank-bearing material, while the long seasoned-wood shaft and dark wraps remain neutral and subordinate.

The metal reads as conventional cool polished steel, while the rank distinction is carried mainly by a decorative cyan circular core and elaborate head silhouette rather than one or two physical Sunsteel construction cues.
The only supernatural emission is a small localized cyan-white core; it does not wash across or turn the full spearhead or shaft into a glowing object.
The realistic painterly dark-fantasy finish, worn shaft and metal surfaces, cold key, restrained warm rim, midnight-charcoal backdrop, and subtle floor plane follow the accepted profile.

No person, text, UI, logo, watermark, rainbow, gold inflation, or full-object glow appears, but the oversized winged spearhead and ornament-led material identity violate the declared no-oversized-silhouettes and no-ornament-as-material-identity constraints.
